sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's new National Electricity Plan (RUPTL) prioritizes 20.9 GW of new renewable capacity by 2030, creating a durable pipeline for geothermal and hydropower developers.
The government's planned carbon tax and mandatory REC (Renewable Energy Certificate) scheme for industrial users will structurally boost demand for clean power certificates and PPAs.
Falling solar module costs and improved battery storage economics are making hybrid solar-plus-storage projects viable in Eastern Indonesia, unlocking a new growth sub-sector.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables sector underperformed today, but the positive moves in US utilities (PCG, XEL) signal defensive rotation. Watch for policy catalysts like the new RUPTL update and potential carbon tax implementation, which could re-rate Indonesian names. Accumulate on weakness, focusing on geothermal and solar plays with clear PPAs.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rural demand recovery is accelerating, driven by government cash transfers and stable palm oil prices, boosting staples like cooking oil and instant noodles.
Premiumization in personal care and home care is durable, with rising middle-class spending on branded hygiene products (e.g., KLIN, FLMC).
E-commerce and direct-to-consumer channels are structurally reshaping FMCG distribution, enabling smaller players (e.g., SOSS, TFCO) to gain share rapidly.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's consumer sector underperformed today (-1.60% ID vs +1.48% US), but watch for selective bottom-fishing in FMCG names like AGAR (+24.75%) and KLIN (+10.00%) as rural demand recovery and Ramadan tailwinds drive near-term upside. Maintain WATCH; entry points may emerge on further weakness.
